open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “Registry's own origin”, given that cookies are scoped by host/domain and path, not by origin or port, and must the cookie carry Secure on host-local HTTP access?
options: Host-only, Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, and Secure always
Host-only, Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, with Secure only on HTTPS deployments
A dedicated Registry hostname plus explicitly declared cookie attributes
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated Registry hostname and a host-only, Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, with Secure on every HTTPS deployment.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation binding digest
open_points.text: “its inputs — for the import, the file's digest and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm, value encoding, field order, treatment of absent values and collection ordering define the confirmation binding?
options: Hash a canonical binary encoding declared by the specification
Hash canonical JSON with declared field and collection ordering
Use an implementation-private serialization and hash
open_points.default_guess: Use a collision-resistant hash of a specification-declared canonical encoding, with fields and collections in their declared deterministic orders.

open_points.subject: A13 session-state concurrency
open_points.text: “The requests of one owner session that change its state … are applied one at a time”
open_points.question: When two such requests arrive concurrently, what determines their serial order, especially for upload versus confirmation, confirmation versus confirmation, and sign-out versus another session-changing request?
options: Order by request arrival
Allow either serial order, provided the result is serializable
Order by a per-session sequence supplied by the forms
open_points.default_guess: Allow either serial order and require the result to equal one complete serial execution.

open_points.subject: A16 uploaded import file
open_points.text: “The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in the store … then it is dropped”
open_points.question: May the personal-data file be written to a temporary filesystem file, or must it remain in memory, and what deletion, permissions and crash-cleanup guarantees does “dropped” require?
options: Memory only
A private temporary file deleted on replacement, acceptance, session end and restart cleanup
Either memory or disk with implementation-defined cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Keep it in a private temporary file accessible only to Registry, remove it on every stated end condition, and clean abandoned import temporaries at startup.

open_points.subject: A16 import required values
open_points.text: “the display name and alias each will arrive under — its v1 name and no alias unless the owner gives others” together with “A brought-in record is malformed when: a required value is missing”
open_points.question: Is required-value validation applied to the source record or to the mapped result, so can an owner-supplied display name repair a picked project whose source display name is missing or blank?
options: Validate source values before mapping; an override cannot repair them
Validate the resulting mapped record; an override may repair them
Refuse such a file at upload before any mapping
open_points.default_guess: Validate the resulting mapped record, allowing the owner-supplied display name to repair the missing source name.

open_points.subject: A16 file and closure digest
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and “closure.file_digest = digest(f)”
open_points.question: What exact bytes and digest algorithm identify the uploaded file, and how is a digest collision handled?
options: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a declared cryptographic algorithm
Digest a canonical parsed representation
Use an implementation-selected digest without collision handling
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact uploaded bytes with a declared collision-resistant algorithm and refuse if one digest is ever associated with different bytes in a live session.

open_points.subject: A16 committed import response
open_points.text: “The import answers once its transaction commits, listing for each Customer it made its v1 value and the customer_ref minted for it” and “While the closure exists, uploading and confirming an import are refused”
open_points.question: How can the owner recover the old-to-new Customer mapping if the transaction commits but its answer is lost, since retry is refused and the closure stores only the file digest?
options: Provide a read of the committed import result
Store the mapping in the migration closure
Make a replay of the same confirmed import return the original result
Accept that the result cannot be recovered through Registry
open_points.default_guess: Persist the result needed for an owner-only read keyed by the migration closure.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup retry
open_points.text: “a failed run is retried at the next run”
open_points.question: If the immediate post-import backup fails, is the retry still a distinct post-import backup, can an ordinary daily backup satisfy it, and when are both due if the next run is the daily run?
options: Retry a distinct post-import run, then also perform the ordinary run
Any later checked backup containing the import satisfies the retry
The next ordinary run is relabelled as the post-import backup
open_points.default_guess: Treat any later checked backup containing the closure as satisfying the protection requirement, without suppressing the ordinary daily schedule.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration namespace
open_points.text: “The configuration holds exactly these items and no other” and “A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start”
open_points.question: What source or namespace counts as Registry's configuration for the unknown-item check—an isolated Registry file/object, all environment variables, or only variables with a Registry prefix?
options: A dedicated Registry configuration object or file
Only environment variables under a declared Registry prefix
The entire process environment
open_points.default_guess: Apply the rule to a dedicated Registry configuration namespace, not to unrelated process environment variables.

open_points.subject: A17 startup check precedence
open_points.text: “The checks run in the order of these rules and the first that fails stops the start”
open_points.question: What is the total check order within each numbered rule and between rule 1's exact-item requirement and rule 5's missing, malformed and unknown-item checks?
options: Declare an explicit ordered list of every individual check
Order items lexically within each numbered rule
Permit any first failure within a numbered rule
open_points.default_guess: Declare a total order: configuration shape, secret presence and representation, length, distinctness, path checks, backup probe, then store opening or creation.

open_points.subject: A17 secret representation
open_points.text: “A secret … is at least 32 bytes long” and “No two secrets are equal”
open_points.question: How are configured textual values converted to bytes for length, equality, authentication and constant-time comparison, and is any Unicode, whitespace or encoding normalization applied?
options: Secrets are raw bytes supplied through a byte-safe encoding
Secrets are UTF-8 text compared without normalization
Secrets are normalized textual values before comparison
open_points.default_guess: Define secrets as exact raw byte strings represented by a declared byte-safe encoding, with no trimming or Unicode normalization.

open_points.subject: A17 startup cleanup
open_points.text: “The backup location must exist and let Registry create and remove a file in it; otherwise the start fails” and “a failed start leaves no file it made”
open_points.question: What must Registry do if the probe file is created but its removal fails, or if creation of a new store leaves a partial file that cannot be removed?
options: Fail and leave the named residue with a diagnostic
Retry cleanup and refuse to serve until cleanup succeeds
Require transactional filesystem creation that cannot leave residue
open_points.default_guess: Fail the start, make bounded cleanup attempts, and report the exact residue path without claiming that no file remains when cleanup itself failed.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and “A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with”
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce-generation rule, file envelope, key interpretation and authentication-failure behavior implement this guarantee?
options: A specification-declared authenticated-encryption format
An implementation-selected authenticated-encryption format fixed per release
Encryption without an authenticated format
open_points.default_guess: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption envelope with a standard AEAD algorithm and a fresh random nonce per backup.

open_points.subject: A18 backup-key digest
open_points.text: “a digest of the key it was made with (never the key)”
open_points.question: Which digest or keyed identifier is recorded, over which exact key bytes, and how are collisions between key identifiers handled?
options: A declared cryptographic hash of the exact key bytes
A random key identifier stored beside the key outside the backup
An implementation-selected digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a declared cryptographic hash of the exact configured key bytes and treat an identifier collision between unequal keys as a fatal configuration or backup error.

open_points.subject: A18 backup key rotation
open_points.text: “When the owner changes the key, older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with”
open_points.question: Where must old backup keys remain available, for how long, and how does the owner select the correct old key when restoring a retained backup?
options: The owner retains every key until all backups using it expire
Registry configuration holds a keyring of current and retained keys
Older backups become unrestorable after key replacement
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to retain each old key outside Registry until no retained backup names its digest.

open_points.subject: A18 missed daily run
open_points.text: “A run that 03:00 found Registry stopped is made when it next starts with its service tokens, if no backup was made that UTC day”
open_points.question: If Registry misses 03:00 on one day and next starts on a later UTC day, is the missed day's run made, is only the current day's backup made, and can a start before the current day's 03:00 create that day's ordinary backup?
options: Never catch up past days; before 03:00 wait for today's scheduled time
Make one catch-up backup immediately and count it for the current UTC day
Make one backup for every missed UTC day
open_points.default_guess: Make one backup immediately on service-enabled startup only if the current day's 03:00 has passed and that day has no ordinary backup; do not synthesize backups for earlier days.

open_points.subject: A18 startup availability
open_points.text: “A run … is made when it next starts with its service tokens” and “the start goes on serving”
open_points.question: Does Registry begin serving before, during or only after the startup cleanup and catch-up backup run completes?
options: Run cleanup and catch-up before serving
Serve after cleanup but run the backup concurrently
Start serving immediately and run all backup work asynchronously
open_points.default_guess: Complete temporary-file cleanup before serving, then serve while the consistent backup runs.

open_points.subject: A18 failed-run consequence
open_points.text: “Every day at the same run — whether the new backup succeeded or not — Registry deletes every backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before” and “a failed run lengthens both [erasure reaching backups and maximum lost changes] by the days until a run succeeds”
open_points.question: Does a failed backup phase lengthen erasure retention when the deletion phase succeeds, and does a failure only in status writing lengthen either guarantee?
options: Only failure of the relevant phase affects its guarantee
Any failed phase makes the entire run ineffective
Deletion and backup success are tracked independently
open_points.default_guess: Track phases independently: successful deletion preserves the erasure bound, successful checked backup preserves the recovery-point bound, and status failure affects neither.

open_points.subject: A18 backup-file namespace
open_points.text: “every one beginning with the prefix the release declares for them” and “removes every file left there under that prefix, and no other file”
open_points.question: How is Registry guaranteed not to delete an unrelated owner file that happens to begin with the temporary prefix, and how are temporary, kept and status names made disjoint?
options: Require a dedicated empty backup directory owned by Registry
Use a Registry-owned subdirectory and disjoint exact filename grammars
Treat every matching file as Registry-owned by convention
open_points.default_guess: Use a Registry-owned subdirectory with disjoint, versioned filename grammars for temporary backups, kept backups and status.

open_points.subject: A04 check stages
open_points.text: Stage (2) checks “the session and its set”, while stage (6) lists “not in the set” as a lifecycle failure
open_points.question: At which stage is a project outside an agent session's set refused, and can any stage 3–5 failure ever be evaluated or reported with it?
options: Only stage 2, hiding every later failure as A10 requires
Only stage 6
Stage 2 for Kernel and stage 6 for owner session-set changes
open_points.default_guess: Treat membership failure on an agent-authority call exclusively as stage 2 and skip every later check.

open_points.subject: A04 action timestamps
open_points.text: “r.last_changed' = now” and “Every action is atomic”
open_points.question: When is “now” sampled for an accepted transaction, and must the record's last-changed instant, archived/restricted/ended instant and audit-entry instant produced by one action be exactly the same value?
options: Sample once at transaction commit and reuse it for every fact of the action
Sample once when the request is admitted
Allow each stored fact to read the clock separately
open_points.default_guess: Sample one UTC instant inside the committing transaction and use it for every timestamp written by that action.

open_points.subject: R0-89 restored store with existing backup directory
open_points.text: “That store begins its own history from the backup” while A18 uses “the kept backups themselves” to decide which days have backups and which backup is newest
open_points.question: After restoring an older store while the backup location still contains backups from the abandoned later history, do those later backups count for scheduling, status, retention and post-import protection, or must Registry distinguish store histories?
options: Count all files in the location regardless of history
Ignore backups not belonging to the current store history
Require the owner to isolate or clean the backup location during restore
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to place the restored store with a backup location isolated from the abandoned history, unless backups carry a store-history identifier that Registry checks.

open_points.subject: R0-89 import after restore
open_points.text: “a store without the migration closure accepts the import”
open_points.question: Does “accepts” mean only that the one-time closure check is open, with all A16 authentication, confirmation, malformed-record and conflict checks still applying, or does it promise that the import succeeds?
options: Only the closure refusal is absent; every A16 check still applies
The same file previously accepted must be accepted again
Any import is accepted when the closure is absent
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it only as reopening eligibility; every A16 check still applies normally.
